rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: 1 mole = 6.022×10²³ entities (Avogadro constant, Nₐ). Molar mass (M) is g·mol⁻¹; for a compound M = Σ(atomic masses).  ·  n (mol) = mass/M = volume(ideal gas, STP)/22.4 L = N/Nₐ.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Law of conservation of mass.** Lavoisier: matter is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction, so total reactant mass equals total product mass.  ·  **Law of definite proportions.** Proust: a pure compound always contains the same elements in the same fixed proportion by mass, whatever its source — water is always 11.1% hydrogen and 88.9% oxygen by mass.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Limiting reactant is the one consumed first; % yield = (experimental/theoretical)×100.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Law of multiple proportions.** Dalton: when two elements form several compounds, the masses of one combining with a fixed mass of the other stand in simple whole-number ratios — CO and CO₂ contain 16 g and 32 g oxygen per 12 g carbon.  ·  **Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.** Gaseous reactants and products at the same temperature and pressure combine in simple whole-number ratios of volume.  ·  **Avogadro's law.** Equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules, which explains Gay-Lussac's volume ratios.
